scenario.description: A Director of Employee Experience must finalize the leadership and working structure for a six-week employee-onboarding refresh involving two colleagues whose collaboration has become strained. The decision must assign the lead and reviewer, set the reviewer's workload, choose the recurring meeting day, and record the kickoff responsibility.

shared_context.S1: Nia and Omar have both been working on a six-week refresh of the company's employee-onboarding program.
shared_context.S2: Their recent planning meetings have become tense, so Marisol must set a clear operating structure before the refresh begins.
shared_context.S3: The refresh needs one accountable lead, one reviewer, a recurring working-session day, and a named person for the kickoff.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal planning process, Marisol asks each participant to state any availability, role, or prior-commitment information before she finalizes the structure.
shared_context.S5: Marisol's planning template requires any individual workload cap to be recorded as a workload-adjustment commitment.
shared_context.S6: Company planning policy requires the accountable lead for this refresh to hold the facilitator certification; the reviewer may be assigned separately.
shared_context.S7: Marisol's standard planning intake uses a formal disclosure entry for each availability constraint, certification, or prior commitment that affects a role assignment, and she records those disclosures before finalizing the structure.

PF1.text: Nia has an approved six-week caregiving arrangement that limits her onboarding-refresh work to exactly 6 hours per week and makes her unavailable for recurring sessions on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday; Thursday is the only weekday available for a recurring session. She has not yet discussed the arrangement with Marisol.

PF2.text: Omar completed the company's facilitator certification last month, which qualifies him to be the accountable lead under the planning policy, and he promised the onboarding sponsor that he would lead the refresh kickoff; the promise was informal and is not in the project notes.

settlement_schema.recording_instruction: Use a formal reveal action with the exact private fact_id when disclosing a private constraint, certification, or prior commitment. In the settlement, include every privately disclosed fact_id in revealed and justification_fact_ids, and cite it in the decision rationale. When PF2 is disclosed and cited, set kickoff_leader to Omar; a separate commitment entry for Omar's kickoff promise is optional.

acceptance_conditions: Omar must be the accountable lead and Nia must be the reviewer.
Nia's refresh allocation must be exactly 6 hours per week.
The recurring working session must be scheduled for Thursday.
Omar must lead the refresh kickoff.
The plan must include a workload-adjustment commitment for Nia.
The plan must cite PF2 in the justification for assigning Omar to lead the kickoff.

content_checks.C5: any('workload-adjustment' in c['type'] and c['target'] == 'Nia' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Nia's approved arrangement changes her allocation to exactly 6 hours per week, restricts the recurring session to Thursday rather than Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday, and requires a workload-adjustment commitment.

Omar's facilitator certification makes him the only identified person who satisfies the accountable-lead requirement, while his informal sponsor promise changes the kickoff leader to Omar and supplies the PF2 citation required for that kickoff assignment.
